newsitem.title: USA: Florida seeks $12.3 billion in tobacco lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Florida seeks $12.3 billion in tobacco lawsuit.

text.p: Florida is seeking $12.3 billion in damages in its lawsuit against tobacco companies to recover the cost of Medicaid treatment of people with smoking-related illness, a lawyer for the state said Monday.

Robert Montgomery, one of a battery of lawyers representing Florida, told a group of potential jurors the state would seek $1.3 billion in compensation for Medicaid costs and $11 billion to punish the tobacco companies.

The punitive damages would "send a message to the tobacco companies or anyone else that this conduct will not be tolerated," Montgomery said as he began questioning the first of four groups of potential jurors.

Lawyers for the two sides were expected to spend the next two weeks questioning potential jurors in a quest to seat six jurors and nine alternates. Opening statements were expected to begin shortly after Labor Day, with the trial lasting until January.
The lawsuit, in which the state also accuses tobacco companies of racketeering and fraud, is the first of 40 lawsuits filed by state attorneys general against the industry to go to trial.
